summary: Mikisaburo Mori was a scholar of sinology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University from around 1930 to 1933 and held positions at Osaka University (circa 1950–1973) and Bukkyo University (circa 1973–1984).

Ming Mei works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned an MPhil at the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin and Qingli Wan, and studied at SOAS University of London under Roderick Whitfield, Tao Wang, Shane McCausland, and Andrey Terentyev.

Ming-Wood Liu worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. He earned his BA at the University of Hong Kong and a PhD at UCLA under Kenneth Kuan Sheng Ch'en, later serving as professor at the University of Hong Kong (~1979–2008).
Mingyu Fu is a Buddhist studies scholar. She completed a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University from circa 2011 to 2013 under the supervision of Shi Huifeng.

Minonori Nishimura specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD at Taisho University under Shunkyo Katsumata and Seiren Matsunami, later serving as associate professor at Taisho University until 2002 and as a researcher at Sanko Research Institute.

Minoru Hara was an Indology, linguistics, and religious studies scholar. Educated at Harvard (PhD) and the University of Tokyo (PhD under Naoshiro Tsuji), he served as professor at the University of Tokyo and president of the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Minoru Kiyota was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Tokyo under teachers including Hajime Nakamura and Akira Hirakawa. He was a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1981.

Minton Warren was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. After studying at Yale University (circa until 1870), he held academic posts at Johns Hopkins University (circa 1879–1899) and Harvard University (circa 1899–1907).

Miranda Shaw works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under doctoral supervisor Masatoshi Nagatomi, teacher Robert A. F. Thurman, traditional teacher Sonam Jorphel Rinpoche, and postdoctoral mentor B. N. Mukherjee.

Mircea Eliade was a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Bucharest and University of Calcutta under Surendranath Dasgupta, holding professorships at Bucharest (~1933–1938), the University of Paris (~1945–1956), and the University of Chicago (~1957–1986).

Mireille Helffer was a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. She held posts at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique as Chargé de Recherche from around 1965 to 1989 and at Paris Nanterre University.

Miri Albahari works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned an MA at the University of Otago and a PhD at the University of Calgary under John A. Baker, later holding posts at the University of Western Australia and UNSW.

Miriam Levering was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. She earned her PhD from Harvard University in 1978 and served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Tennessee from circa 1982 to 2011.
Mirjan Damaška studied at the University of Ljubljana from around 1956 to 1960. He held a post at Yale Law School from around 1976 to 2023.

Mitsuji Fukunaga was a sinologist and philosopher who studied at Kyoto University (~1939–1942). He held academic posts at the University of Kitakyushu, Kyoto University, the University of Tokyo (professor ~1982–1989), and Kansai University.
Mitsutoshi Moriguchi is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed doctoral coursework at Taisho University and held an appointment there as a lecturer in 1987.
Mitsuyo Demoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at Kyoto University and held a position at the University of Marburg.

Mitsuyoshi Saigusa was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1947–1950), he held posts at Kokugakuin University (~1969–1975) and the University of Tsukuba (~1975–1987), where he was named professor emeritus.

Mitsuyuki Ishida was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1932–1937). He served as a professor at Ryukoku University from around 1949 to 1982 and at Shitennoji University from around 1982 to 1989.

Mizuho Okita specializes in Indology and religious studies. She earned a BA at Tokai University and studied at Gakushuin University under doctoral supervisor Atsuhiko Yoshida, later serving as a part-time lecturer at Meisei University.
